# onpager_user_notification_defaults (Resource)

Manage the tenant template for personal contacts and notification policies. OnPager applies eligible sections when creating a user or granting individual access, before the API returns.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "telegram_channel_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of an existing enabled, globally visible Telegram bot channel."
}

locals {
  telegram_contact_slot_id = "787e409c-5bbf-420f-bf42-98d0daea3263"
}

resource "onpager_user_notification_defaults" "example" {
  enabled = true
  contacts = [{
    id                   = local.telegram_contact_slot_id
    channel_id           = var.telegram_channel_id
    display_name         = "Telegram"
    require_verification = true
  }]

  policies = {
    default = {
      configured = true
      steps      = [{ kind = "notify", contact_id = local.telegram_contact_slot_id }]
    }
    important = {
      configured = true
      steps = [
        { kind = "notify", contact_id = local.telegram_contact_slot_id },
        { kind = "wait", wait_seconds = 60 },
        { kind = "notify", contact_id = local.telegram_contact_slot_id },
      ]
    }
  }
}

variable "initial_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "onpager_user" "example" {
  depends_on = [onpager_user_notification_defaults.example]

  login            = "example-user"
  display_name     = "Example user"
  initial_password = var.initial_password
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `contacts` (Attributes List) Complete list of contact slots. Use an empty list to configure no contacts. Each slot and delivery channel may appear once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contacts))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether OnPager applies the template to eligible users. Enabling a populated template also schedules updates to inherited sections for existing users. Disabling it preserves the template content and existing personal settings.
- `policies` (Attributes) Both complete personal notification policy templates. Each policy is required and may be unconfigured or explicitly empty. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton ID and import identifier, always `tenant`. Configure one resource per tenant.
- `revision` (Number) Server-assigned template revision, initially zero. Each committed replacement advances this counter. Concurrent saves take effect in commit order.

<a id="nestedatt--contacts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contacts`

Required:

- `channel_id` (String) Known enabled, globally available delivery-channel UUID. A webhook's channel UUID is distinct from its webhook UUID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `display_name` (String) Contact label from 1 through 200 Unicode characters, without surrounding whitespace.
- `id` (String) Stable slot UUID chosen for this template. Policy notify steps reference this ID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

Optional:

- `lookup_attribute` (String) Identity attribute used to resolve the recipient, such as `email` or `preferred_username`, when supported by the channel. Omission, null and an empty string select no lookup attribute. Channels offering lookup attributes require an explicit supported value.
- `require_verification` (Boolean) Whether enrollment requires verification. Omission or null defaults to true. False requires a channel supporting automatic verification. Telegram and Discord require true in the template. An authorized administrator can separately confirm a known bot recipient.


<a id="nestedatt--policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies`

Required:

- `default` (Attributes) Template for default-importance notifications. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies--default))
- `important` (Attributes) Template for important notifications. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies--important))

<a id="nestedatt--policies--default"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies.default`

Required:

- `configured` (Boolean) Whether eligible users inherit this policy. Set to false with an empty step list to skip this policy. Set to true with an empty step list to publish an explicitly empty policy.
- `steps` (Attributes List) Complete ordered list of notification and wait steps. Use an empty list when configured is false. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies--default--steps))

<a id="nestedatt--policies--default--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies.default.steps`

Required:

- `kind` (String) Step kind, either `notify` or `wait`.

Optional:

- `contact_id` (String) UUID of a contact slot in this template. Required for notify. Omit or set to null for wait.
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Wait duration in whole seconds, from 1 through 9223372036. Required for wait. Omit or set to null for notify.



<a id="nestedatt--policies--important"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies.important`

Required:

- `configured` (Boolean) Whether eligible users inherit this policy. Set to false with an empty step list to skip this policy. Set to true with an empty step list to publish an explicitly empty policy.
- `steps` (Attributes List) Complete ordered list of notification and wait steps. Use an empty list when configured is false. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies--important--steps))

<a id="nestedatt--policies--important--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies.important.steps`

Required:

- `kind` (String) Step kind, either `notify` or `wait`.

Optional:

- `contact_id` (String) UUID of a contact slot in this template. Required for notify. Omit or set to null for wait.
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Wait duration in whole seconds, from 1 through 9223372036. Required for wait. Omit or set to null for notify.

## How the template applies

Configure one resource per tenant. When Terraform creates a local user, Control
saves the user and eligible sections of the enabled template in the same
transaction. They are readable when create returns, before the user's first
sign-in. The example uses `depends_on` to publish the template before creating
the user in the same apply.

If the user needs additional permissions, an individual role grant or manual
group membership applies newly eligible sections before that operation returns.
Permissions granted solely through an OIDC group take effect at sign-in.
Publishing an enabled template with configured sections also schedules a
background update for existing users. Each policy inherits later revisions
until the user edits it, including explicitly clearing its steps. Language
and time zone follow the user's profile preferences independently.

Each contact slot has a stable UUID of its own and references an enabled,
globally visible channel by UUID. For an outgoing webhook use its delivery
channel UUID. A policy's `notify` step references the contact slot UUID.
Terraform sends these references together in a single request, in the order
given. OnPager validates channel availability and lookup capabilities at write
time. A policy can reference a draft contact. For bot delivery before sign-in,
an administrator with `user_bot_contacts.manage` can set a known `recipient_id`
and `verified = true` with a [user bot contact](user_bot_contact.md). A login or
email alone does not confirm a bot recipient.

Disabling the template preserves its saved contacts and policies. A policy with
`configured = false` and `steps = []` skips initialization of that section.
With `configured = true`, an empty list explicitly initializes an empty policy.

## Import

Use the literal ID `tenant`. Create reads the current template first. An
enabled template, any contact slot, or either configured policy requires
explicit import, even when disabled or when a configured policy has zero steps.
An empty, disabled template can be managed regardless of its current revision.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_user_notification_defaults.example
  id = "tenant"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_user_notification_defaults.example tenant
```

## Writes and destroy

Apply sends the complete template to `/v1/settings/user-notification-defaults`.
The encoded request body is limited to 128 KiB. Control returns the saved
template and its revision. The initial revision is
zero. The revision records changes and supplies no write precondition.
Concurrent writes take effect in commit order, including changes from the UI.

Destroy publishes a disabled template with an empty contact list and both
policies unconfigured with empty step lists. The tenant setting remains
readable after reset. Previously initialized profiles and enrollment history
survive. A failed reset or read retains the managed resource in Terraform state.

## Permissions

Import and refresh require `tenant_settings.read`. Initial apply also uses this
grant for the ownership check. Writes and reset require `tenant_settings.update`.
PATs and service accounts can use these tenant grants. The example also needs
`users.create` and `users.read` to provision the user, and `users.deactivate`
to destroy it. Personal restore, retry and code-based enrollment use the
user's session.
